title: Catalog ingestion validation, pin semantics, and compatibility annotations
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Clarify and lock the acceptance criteria, validation rules, and runtime semantics for new open-model ingestion into the Model Catalog. Deliver a clear spec for engineer and design teams that reduces ambiguity around version pinning, compatibility annotations, and automated fallback behavior so that new community models can be safely advertised in hosted and dedicated deployments.
problem_statement: Current model intake checks are underspecified: teams onboard models with varying manifest fields, inconsistent pinning expectations, and ambiguous compatibility notes. This creates runtime surprises (incompatible kernels, unexpected quantization profiles) and increases rollback toil. We need a single source of truth for validation and pin semantics to reduce failed serving rollouts and support automated fallback paths.
goals: Define a strict ingestion manifest v2 that enumerates required fields and optional compatibility hints
Specify pinning semantics (hard/soft pin, TTL, auto-refresh) and how runtime respects pins across hosted/dedicated/private deployments
Provide deterministic compatibility scoring and a small set of standardized annotations to be surfaced in the Console and API
Define acceptance tests and rollout checklists so that PM/Eng/Design can sign off on a model being added to the catalog
scope: Create manifest v2 schema and validator (fields, types, canonical names, example manifests)
Define pinning modes: hard_pin, soft_pin, and ephemeral_pin along with TTL and rollback triggers
Define 6 compatibility annotations (arch_match, dtype_support, kv_cache_expectation, kv_layout_hint, quantization_profile, seq_length_rating)
Document runtime behaviors when a requested model variant is unavailable (fallback order and logging semantics)
Acceptance criteria and an automated test harness that runs ingestion validations against a sample set of community models
out_of_scope: Implementing full runtime auto-translation of model weights (outside prototype spec)
Major Console UI redesign — UI surface will be minimal (prominent annotations only)
Changes to billing or pricing models tied to pin types
requirements: Manifest v2 must include: model_id, version, architecture, tokenizer_spec, default_quant_profile, supported_dtypes, recommended_max_ctx, checksum, provenance_url
Ingestion validator returns structured error codes and remediation hints (ERR_ARCH_MISMATCH, ERR_MISSING_TOKENIZER, WARN_QUANT_LOSS)
Pin semantics API: POST /catalog/pin accepts {model_id, version, mode, ttl_days} and returns authoritative expiry timestamp
Runtime must enforce hard_pin by refusing automatic variant fallback; soft_pin allows fallback but emits higher-severity audit events
Compatibility score computed as weighted metric (arch_match=0.4, dtype_support=0.2, quant_profile=0.2, kv_cache=0.2) and exposed as a 0-100 integer
A minimal annotations glossary is included in the manifest validator output and surfaced in model catalog entries
Automated test harness runs a set of 25 community models through validator and simulates runtime selection with both hosted and dedicated routing rules
acceptance_criteria: Validator implements manifest v2 and passes the 25-model ingestion test set with at most 2 warn-level issues across the set
Pin API exists and supports hard_pin/soft_pin/ephemeral_pin; TTL semantics validated by unit tests (expiry, renewal, and race conditions)
Runtime respects hard_pin for both hosted and dedicated modes in a simulated integration test and emits the defined audit event with the correct schema
Compatibility score appears in the Console model detail page and in the /catalog/list API response; values are stable for identical manifests
Runbook created for common remediation paths and rollback triggers with clear owners (Eng SRE, Model Onboarding, PM)
Design review complete for Console display of annotations and pin controls; accessibility checklist is green
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize manifest schema v2 and publish spec to Confluence; ship validator prototype to catalog ingestion service (feature flag off)
Week 2: Add pin API endpoints behind feature flag; integrate validator into ingestion pipeline (flag gated); run full ingestion test harness
Week 3: Run staged runtime integration tests for hosted and dedicated routing; iterate on scoring weights if false positives observed
Week 4: Enable feature flag for limited customer beta (internal Redwood customers + 3 external partners); monitor metrics for fallback events and serve latency regressions
Post-beta: Address issues, perform security review if required, and schedule GA with communications and migration guidance
dependencies: ENG-41234: Catalog ingestion service refactor (streamlined validators)
ENG-42901: Runtime fallback and audit-event plumbing
DES-9021: Console annotation UI and pin control components
SEC-114: Review of manifest provenance handling and checksum verification
